substantiveCorrections.basis: Both book editions quantify the polynomial indeterminate z by mistake. The cited Granville author-hosted original paper, printed4/PDF2, quantifies the constant a in (x+a)^n≡x^n+a and explicitly distinguishes polynomial identities from evaluations at integer x. Only z→a in the bound is repaired; book lower bound0 and its other hypotheses retained.

substantiveCorrections.basis: English states that the probabilistic algorithm finds a proof of primality when n is prime. Its randomized running-time guarantee does not turn its successful output into merely a probable-prime judgement.
